title: The Final Draw on Reconstruction Contracts
content:
The final draw of a Reconstruction contract is the draw at the substantial completion milestone, requested once the final walkthrough has recorded substantial completion.

## Scope

For the substantial completion draw, and only for that draw, the requested amount is worked out under the final draw rules. Every other draw requests the milestone's percentage of the current contract sum, which is the contract amount plus signed additive change orders less signed deductive change orders as of the request date, and the contract signing draw is also capped at the tier's deposit maximum, as the base draw rule states.

On tiers with retainage every draw before the final one withholds the retainage percentage as the base draw rule states, and that withheld total is requested as the retainage release draw once the tier's retainage release days have passed after substantial completion, together with the final retainage and every other amount the final draw holds back once each is released; the retainage withheld from earlier draws is requested there and only there. Every amount the final draw holds back is requested as the contract's retainage release draw: the tier's retainage once the tier's retainage release days have passed after substantial completion, and every other held amount once it is released.

## When the amount is fixed

The final draw's requested amount is fixed only after no change order proposal other than a deductive one stands on the contract awaiting the customer's signature; a proposal whose amount worked out under the change order signature rule falls below the tier's change order minimum is not counted, because it cannot be written.

Put as a reading of the contract's records on the request date: while any proposal other than a deductive one stands on the contract awaiting the customer's signature, the final draw's requested amount is not yet fixed; a proposal whose amount worked out under the change order signature rule falls below the tier's change order minimum does not count, because it cannot be written.

A final draw that works out to less than half a cent is not requested, and every amount it holds back is requested as the retainage release draw as stated above.

## Invocation: `request_final_draw_345d01eb`

`request_final_draw_345d01eb` is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. It requests a milestone draw, the final draw included, on a Reconstruction contract: one call records a new draw request at the named milestone, dated today, carrying the draw's sequence number, who funds it, the lien waiver delivered with it, its due date and the amount requested. The contract balance does not change; the draw appears among the contract's draw requests and can then be paid or posted against.

### Parameters

- `rebuild_contract_id` — the reference number of the Reconstruction contract the draw is requested on, as returned by the contract lookup.
- `draw_milestone` — the contract milestone the draw bills, exactly one of: `contract_signing` (the deposit draw at signing); `framing_complete` (framing finished); `rough_in_complete` (rough-in finished); `drywall_complete` (drywall finished); `finishes_complete` (finishes installed); `substantial_completion` (the final draw after the final walkthrough); `retainage_release` (the release of amounts withheld or held back from earlier draws).
- `draw_number` — the sequence number of this draw on the contract, an integer counting every draw requested on the contract including this one, starting at 1.
- `funding_route` — who funds the draw, exactly one of: `customer` (the owner pays the draw from their own funds); `carrier_direct` (the draw is paid from carrier payments that reached the company); `mortgagee_release` (the draw is released from the mortgagee's loss-draft account).
- `lien_waiver_type` — the lien waiver delivered with the request, exactly one of: `none` (no lien waiver accompanies the request); `conditional_progress` (a conditional progress lien waiver accompanies an interim draw); `conditional_final` (a conditional final lien waiver accompanies the final draw).
- `due_date` — the date the draw is due, written YYYY-MM-DD in the company's local calendar, or an empty string when the draw carries no due date.
- `requested_amount` — the amount requested on the draw, in US dollars, a number with exactly 2 decimal places; any further digits are rounded to the cent, half up.

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the new draw request reference (a text id beginning "rbd_"), the milestone billed, the draw number, the funding route and the amount requested in US dollars with 2 decimals. The presence of the draw reference means the request was recorded.
